chap: 1 title
texts: what each layer depends on, what the planner outputs, and the HACC post-map
arm M2b, two training seeds (s0, s1)  |  banked checkpoints and banked per-window plans, CPU re-read  |  T1-class open loop (NOT closed loop); interventions are diagnostics
Every layer also reads the NAV command (FOLLOW / TURN_L / TURN_R and the distance to the next turn), ego motion and the camera tokens.
1   Who listens to what?  Which input does each layer actually depend on (causal, one input swapped at a time)?
2   Does the trajectory follow the nav command, and through which layer?  (nav injected at one layer at a time)
3   What does the planner's output look like against the human path, the kinematic prior P10 and the earlier blends?

4   NEW in v3:  does HACC, a zero-training per-step blend of the model's plan and P10, dominate P10 at both training
seeds, and where does the gain come from?

5   NEW in v4 (chapter 7):  T1-kin, the model run on its OWN executed motion, replanning every 2 s (self-action OPEN
loop, NOT closed loop): does HACC still beat the floor run the same way, and which gap stays open?

Four windows were declared before anything was rendered (SELECTION_V2.md, unchanged): JUNCTION #1131, CURVE #654, NO-TURN #763, FAILURE #2158.  Every
window panel is seed 0; seed 1 sits in a summary card.

Tier of chapters 1-6: T1-class open loop (own held outputs; NOT closed loop).  The model reads its own held outputs; nothing it does feeds back into
the scene.  Interventions replace an input: they show dependence, not skill.
Baseline: P10 is the programme's own kinematic floor (it extrapolates ego motion and ignores the scene).  It is not the state of the art, and no external benchmark is shown.
Estimator: paired episode-cluster bootstrap, B = 2,000, 141 episodes (answers 'another draw of EPISODES' only); training variance = the two seeds side by side; inference is deterministic.

Cell = layer's output change when that input is swapped (S, O: metres; T: macro-F1 drop).   Heavy frame = the row's largest ratio n.   * = listens at both seeds.   Hatched = not an input.

HOW TO READ IT.  Take ONE input of ONE layer (scene, ego, nav, speed limit, S's checkpoints, T's code, tick ages), swap it for the
value from a window of ANOTHER episode, and measure how much that layer's own output gets worse.  A big cell = the layer depends on
that input.  Left: training seed 0.  Right: seed 1.

3  Nav counterfactual: what happens to the plan when ONLY the nav input changes?

For each of the four pre-declared windows the nav input is REPLACED by a synthetic command and the model is run through its
own chain S -> T -> O.
Commands:  FOLLOW,  TURN LEFT,  TURN RIGHT, each with d_next = 30 m and 'arguments valid' = 1.
Everything else is the window's own: ego motion, speed limit, camera tokens, held ages.
(a)  nav injected at all three layers

Read for each case:
  - the 6 s plan (dots every 1 s)
  - S's three checkpoints
  - T's lateral decision (argmax)

Headline number D6 = how far the TURN plans
end (at 6 s) from the FOLLOW plan, in metres,
averaged over TURN LEFT and TURN RIGHT.

INTERVENTION on the model's input, open loop; not driving.  A TURN command on a straight road is something the road does not
offer: the experiment shows what the model DEPENDS on, not what is correct.

SELECTION_V2.md section 2 (pre-declared before any render).  Plans in this segment are the model's own plan B, BEFORE the HACC post-map.  Command vectors in the model's nav encoding [FOLLOW, TURN_L, TURN_R one-hot, d_next/100, args_valid].  Layers are run
through the model's own run_s / run_t / run_o (tip 9a6551d5).

3  Nav counterfactual: how far each command moves the 6 s plan, per injection point, both seeds

D6 in metres  (top: seed 0  |  seed 1)
L-R lateral spread (below)

D6 = mean over {TURN LEFT, TURN RIGHT} of the distance at 6 s between that plan and the FOLLOW plan, same injection point.  Eval-wide, with nav at all three layers, T's lateral argmax equals the command in 94 / 52 /
62 % of windows (FOLLOW / TURN_L / TURN_R, seed 0) and 90 / 54 / 73 % (seed 1).

Eval-wide (bottom row), both seeds: O only (about 1 m) < T only (about 4 m) < all three layers ~ S only (about 10-11 m).  The command moves the
trajectory through S's checkpoints and T's code; O's own nav token is nearly inert.  On the four windows (examples), T's lateral decision follows the
command (nav at all three layers) in 23 of 24 cases (4 windows x 2 seeds x 3 commands); the exceptions: FAILURE (worst) s1 TURN_R.  Single windows can
flip the O-only / T-only order: T only < O only on JUNCTION seed 1.

Artifacts: viz3/data/cf_windows.npz (a byte-identical copy of viz2's; 4 windows, both seeds), viz3/data/cf_evalwide.json (a copy; 2,399 windows; episode-cluster bootstrap B = 2,000, 141 episodes: another draw of EPISODES; the two training seeds side by side;
inference deterministic).  Tier T1-class open loop; intervention on the model's input, not driving.

4  Better plans: what HACC closes, and what is still NOT better
1   Accel and curvature gap to P10: closed

Before HACC, H was separated-WORSE than P10 on the accel row (accel MAE, H - P10:
+0.104 s0, +0.066 s1 m/s^2).  HACC is separated-better at both seeds.
2   What is NOT better, and what it costs

(a) vs the model's own plan B: the consistency cost remains.
CONSISTENCY(a) 'any' (share of windows violating a GT-derived constraint; lower is
better):
   HACC - B   s0 +0.0763 [+0.0450, +0.1092] sep.
              s1 +0.0550 [+0.0317, +0.0779] sep.
   HACC - P10 s0 -0.0750 [-0.1017, -0.0496] sep.
              s1 -0.0463 [-0.0684, -0.0242] sep.

(b) vs H: a small loss on three rows.
   cross-track MAE (m)  HACC - H   s0 +0.0274 [+0.0148, +0.0409] sep.
                                   s1 +0.0138 [+0.0004, +0.0272] sep.
   ADE6 (m)             HACC - H   s0 +0.0151 [-0.0030, +0.0320] n.s.
                                   s1 +0.0313 [+0.0026, +0.0586] sep.
   FDE6 (m)             HACC - H   s0 +0.1195 [+0.0411, +0.1966] sep.
                                   s1 +0.1886 [+0.0652, +0.3092] sep.

(c) vs P10: distance keeping (headway, time-gap) is NOT separated at either seed
(next segment).
(d) at 5.2-5.8 s the accel error is still ABOVE P10 (HACC - P10 +0.233 s0, +0.127 s1
m/s^2; next segment).

Honest status: HACC meets the dominance read against the prior at both seeds (no row separated-worse; next segment) and closes the
acceleration and curvature gap that H left.  What it gives back is small against H (cross-track, FDE6, and at seed 1 ADE6) and the
consistency cost against B stays.  Distance keeping is not separated from P10.

Source: hacc/score_M2b_s{0,1}.json (paired.HACC_minus_{P10,H}, consistency.paired.HACC_minus_{B,P10}, single); hacc/accel_profile.json (late-horizon band).  Paired episode-cluster bootstrap, B = 2,000, 141 episodes (another draw of EPISODES); two seeds side by
side.  Tier T1-class open loop (own held outputs; NOT closed loop).  H - P10 (before HACC) from hspec/RESULT_V8F_HSPEC.md via viz3/data/tables.json.

texts: TanitAD v8F-mini  |  evidence video v4 (HACC + T1-kin)  |  numbers read from banked artifacts, paths in VIDEO_NOTES_V4.md  |  CPU, dev box
T1-class open loop (own held outputs; NOT closed loop)
5  Dominance: the mechanism (one lever: how the per-step blend weight is fitted)
HACC = P + w (tau - P)  |  w is 30 x 2 numbers per seed, a fixed function of the step index  |  zero network training

H (HBLEND):  w fitted on POSITION error only, then forced to be non-decreasing in
time.

HACC:  w fitted on position error PLUS lambda x the second-difference (acceleration)
error, bounded to [0, 1], NO monotone constraint.  lambda is picked by a train-only
rule (lambda* = 9,998 seed 0, 36,931 seed 1).

Both: one weight per plan step and axis (30 x 2 per model), fitted on TRAINING
windows only; at inference w depends on the step index alone and P is the deployed
prior, so there is no scene read, no situation-classifier output, no label.

A DESCRIPTIVE reading (not an ablation: the accel term and the dropped monotone
constraint changed together):
  along weight, steps 10 -> 14 (2.0 -> 2.8 s), seed 0:  H 0.12 -> 0.50,  HACC 0.20
-> 0.41
  seed 1:  H 0.14 -> 0.59,  HACC 0.22 -> 0.46.
H's steep ramp sits where its accel error peaked (yellow band); HACC ramps more
gently and is not monotone elsewhere (steps where w decreases: along 4 / 7, cross 18
/ 18, seed 0 / seed 1).

First steps of the cross axis: HACC's w jumps 1 / 0 / 1 / 0 because mean |tau - P|
there is only 0.018 m (seed 0, step 4): the weight is barely identified there and
moves the plan by that much on average at most.

The mechanism in one sentence: HACC is the same one-line blend as H, but its per-step weight is fitted with an acceleration term in the objective
and without the monotone constraint, so it can ramp gently where the model's plan turns and dip where it is rough.  Written as a prediction before
any number was seen (PREREG_V8F_HACC); the result is what dominates P10, the explanation is descriptive.

Source: hacc/weights_HACC_M2b_s{0,1}.json, hblend/weights_M2b_s{0,1}.json (w_along_by_step, w_cross_by_step), hacc/READ.json (lambda*), viz3/data/aux3.json (mean |tau - P| from hblend/score_*_perwindow.npz).  Tier T1-class open loop (own held outputs; NOT closed
loop).  Weights were fitted on the 9,582 training windows of HBLEND's fit set; no eval window enters a fit or a selection.

chap: 5 dominance over the kinematic prior
texts: TanitAD v8F-mini  |  evidence video v4 (HACC + T1-kin)  |  numbers read from banked artifacts, paths in VIDEO_NOTES_V4.md  |  CPU, dev box
T1-class open loop (own held outputs; NOT closed loop)
5  Dominance: what travels with this result
read these before quoting the dominance row

T1-class open loop: the model's own held outputs scored against the logged human path.  NOT closed loop; nothing here shows the plan being followed by a
vehicle.

P10 is the programme's kinematic floor (it extrapolates ego motion and ignores the scene).  Beating it is a statement about our own floor, not about the state
of the art; no external benchmark is shown.

Paired episode-cluster bootstrap, B = 2,000, 141 episodes: it answers 'would another draw of EPISODES say this?' only.  Training variance is read only from the
two seeds side by side; F = |ADE6(s0) - ADE6(s1)| of B = 0.1207 m is the seed floor.  Inference is deterministic, so there is no inference-seed floor.

PRIMARY-KEEP asks that HACC stays within F/2 = +0.06037 m of H on ADE6.  Seed 0: HACC - H +0.0151 [-0.0030, +0.0320] (not separated).  Seed 1: +0.0313 [+0.0026,
+0.0586]: HACC is SEPARATED-WORSE than H by 0.0313 m ADE6, and passes the bar by only 0.0018 m.
Headway and time-gap are not separated from P10 at either seed (LEAD-VIOL is separated at seed 0 only).  Nothing is separated-worse.

HACC touches the 6 s plan only.  T's decision heads and S's checkpoints are the banked B arrays, so HACC - H is exactly 0 on the strategic block.  The STRATEGIC
family is IN FORCE for v8F (PI-V8F-2026-10-17; R72 / R73): S at its deployed (held) schedule still loses to the nav-only baseline at 50 m (next segment).
HACC is not yet folded into forward_infer (its own landing, with tests), and the next tier (D-V8F-T1KIN-1) needs a PI go for the pooled eval cache.

Dominance over P10 is measured at both training seeds on the pre-registered read.  It is a T1-class open-loop result against our own floor; the
cost against H is small but real at seed 1, and the strategic layer is a separate open item that HACC does not touch.

Source: hacc/READ.json (PRIMARY_KEEP, KEEP_bar_m, F_exact_m), RESULT_V8F_HACC.md sections 0, 4 and 8, PREREG_V8F_HACC.md (committed next step).  Tier T1-class open loop (own held outputs; NOT closed loop).

Against chapters 1-6 the model no longer reads the human's logged motion: it reads its OWN executed motion
tier T1-kin = self-action OPEN loop  |  NOT closed loop: the cameras are the human's recorded frames, nothing re-renders the scene

Every 2 s (m = 10 steps of 0.2 s) the
model REPLANS.

At each replan its ego state (speed,
history, odometry, the route countdown)
is rebuilt from what it has itself
EXECUTED so far, not from the logged
human motion.

The floor P10 (the programme's kinematic
prior, which ignores the scene) is run
the same way, in its own loop, on the
same windows.

Score: ADE6 of each executed 6 s track
against the human's logged path.

CAUSAL:  the camera frames are the
human's logged frames.  The speed bucket
is built from the past 4 s of measured
speed only (logged up to the window
start, the model's own executed speed
after it): no future row, no label.

STRICT:  as CAUSAL, and the cameras are
frozen: the FIRST frame of the window is
held for all 6 s.

checkpoints), two training seeds, s0 and
s1.

before any T1 number per window was read

(logged for CAUSAL, frozen for STRICT),
and a bird's-eye view of the human's
path (GT), the model's executed track
and the floor's executed track, growing
in time, replan ticks marked.

windows, three result cards (CAUSAL,

from the T1-grid windows whose GT mean speed is at least 5 m/s (1,911
of 2,399 windows; 1,907 candidates after excluding the four of rule 1).
GT mean speed = mean over the 30 knots of |g[k] - g[k-1]| / 0.2 s.

Where the floor is better, the caption says so and the window stays.

Why a rule, and why these windows are NOT a sample of the typical window

The four windows of chapters 3-6 were chosen there as the median of their stratum and the worst of all windows.  The three draws are random among
windows that move (at least 5 m/s), so that the executed tracks have a length to compare.  Slow and standing windows are in the evaluation (and in the
distribution card), just not in the draw.  A window is an example; the distribution card and the result cards are the evidence.

The lateral deficit is real at speed, and it is in curvature, not in lateral acceleration or
position.  Masking the speeds where millimetres dominate shrinks the curvature excess by 30–37 %
(+0.030 to +0.021, +0.013 to +0.008 1/m), but a part remains at speed.

at-speed excess arises in the LOOP (state, seams), not in a single plan.  The box-2 lateral
training lever is blocked on box-2 compute.
